diagnostic_evidence.quote: Similar constructions can be carried out to obtain analogues of higher-order

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract says the main result is that such formulae can be explicitly constructed for a wide class of functions and have the same accuracy as Newton-Cotes formulae on the same nodes. The paper proves error orders only for the 2-node rule (o(h^2)) and the 3-node rule (o(h^4)). The 3-node bound is weaker than the O(h^5) of Simpson's rule, and the paper never states or proves O(h^5) for it. For more nodes it only asserts that 'similar constructions can be carried out'. Corollary 'cor:added-4' covers only the linear case. The nonlinear higher-order construction would need cancellations of higher partial derivatives of an arbitrary affinely exact symmetric q_1, and none of that is shown. The 'wide class' is also restricted to globally bijective f^*:R->R.

failure_location.quote: explicitly constructed for a wide class of functions, and have the same

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the abstract and conclusion to what is proved (2- and 3-node rules with o(h^2) and o(h^4) errors), or supply the general-n argument showing the nonlinear Richardson-type combinations reach the Newton-Cotes order.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised general accuracy statement for arbitrary node counts is unsupported. Only n=2 and n=3 are established, at the orders the paper states.
issues.title: Abstract claims Newton-Cotes accuracy for the constructed rules, but only the 2- and 3-node cases are treated
issues.why_classification: Narrowing the claim needs no new proof but drops the advertised general-n statement. Keeping that statement would need a contained new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\bar{f}$ with $f(a)$ in the range of $f^*$ the equalities $q(\bar{f})=f(a)$

issues.failure_explanation: Scalable exactness only forces q(f̄)=f(a) and q^{(0,1)}(f̄)=1/2 at diagonal points λ f̄* with λ in the interval (λ_-,λ_+), a neighbourhood of f*(a). Exactness for all h>0 constrains q only on the region swept by (λ f*(a), λ f*(a+h)). Outside it q can be changed smoothly (for example multiplied by a cutoff) while keeping scalable exactness. Such a q gives O(h) error for f with f(a) far from f*(a), so 'for all f in C^2' is false. In the affine lemma the proof itself restricts to 'f(a) in the range of f*', yet the statement is for all f. The paper's own q_1 for e^x is undefined for f(a)<=0. Corollary 'cor:pders' states the identities 'for all f̄' with the same unjustified extension. Theorem 'thm:construct' claims o(h^4) for every f in C^4(R) although q_1 is defined only for f-values in the range of f*.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the conclusions to f with f(a) in (λ_-,λ_+)·f*(a) for the scalable case and in the range of f* for the affine case. Restrict Corollary cor:pders and the error claim of Theorem thm:construct to f with node values in that range.
issues.overall_effect: The 'no worse than the trapezoidal rule on general functions' conclusion and the order claims hold only for integrands whose values at a lie in the neighbourhood or range where q is controlled. The stated universal scope is false.
issues.title: Local conditions on q (near the ray of f*) are extended to all q-arguments and all f in C^2
issues.why_classification: The repair is a domain restriction with the same proofs. It still weakens the advertised 'all f' result, so it is more than a routine local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: to reduce the integration error of the trapezoidal rule by using the known

issues.failure_explanation: The value q^{(0,2)} = -(1/6) f*''/f*'^2 is derived only at f̄* = (f*(a), f*(a)). The Taylor expansion of q around f(b)=f(a) needs q^{(0,2)} at (f(a), f(a)) for arbitrary f(a). Since q is homogeneous of degree 1 along the exactness rays, q^{(0,2)}(λ f̄*) = λ^{-1} q^{(0,2)}(f̄*). The stated coefficient is therefore correct only for f(a)=f*(a). Check with f*=e^x and f=λe^x: the exact-rule expansion has coefficient -(f_1-f_0)^2/(12 f_0), not -(f_1-f_0)^2/12. The proposed improved trapezoidal rule, built for functions close to multiples of f*, mis-scales the correction by λ. For f=2e^x on [0,h] the corrected rule has error -h^3/6 versus the trapezoid's +h^3/6, so there is no improvement. The corollary also omits the hypothesis f*(a)≠0 that its proof (via q^{(0,1)}=1/2) needs.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the coefficient by the scale-covariant one, -(1/12) f*''(a)/f*'(a)^2 · f*(a)/f(a), which follows from applying the same computation to λ f* or from degree-1 homogeneity. Add the hypothesis f*(a)≠0 and update the improved-rule formula.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's formula is wrong except at the single scale f(a)=f*(a). The suggested improved trapezoidal rule does not reduce the error for general multiples λ f*.

issues.why_classification: A short local correction using homogeneity fixes the formula and the derived rule while keeping all claims and the method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: an $n$-point quadrature formula that is exact on polynomials of order $n-1$
and hence demanding that the Taylor expansion of $\hat{I}[f]$ matches that of

issues.failure_explanation: Exactness on polynomials of degree <= n-1 requires matching the h f(a) and h^2 f'(a) terms, i.e. sum_k alpha_k = 1. This is not among the (n-1) equations j=2..n, which instead match terms up to f^{(n)}. The proof never shows the extra condition holds, and it is not automatic for a general node set. For odd n it follows only because the nodal polynomial is antisymmetric about 1/2, so that the 'missing' combination of equations has right-hand side 1; this is the only place oddness of n matters, and it is never invoked. The independence claim 'rows are polynomials of different orders' is also not a valid argument for n-1 sample points. The rows are xi^j - xi + 1, and independence needs a separate argument using node 0 and the constraint at xi=1. Hence the conclusion that the unique solution is exact to degree n-1 and equals the Newton-Cotes rule is not established.

failure_location.quote: which has a unique solution since the rows are polynomials of different orders

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the equation sum alpha_k = 1 and prove it is implied by the j=2..n system for odd n (nodal-polynomial antisymmetry). Give a correct proof of invertibility of the system, or state the full n-equation system and prove it is consistent and uniquely solvable.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed recovery of Boole's and the higher-order rules from trapezoidal combinations rests on an unproved consistency of an over-determined system and an invalid uniqueness argument.
issues.title: Proof of Newton-Cotes recovery omits the normalisation equation and gives no valid independence/consistency argument
issues.why_classification: A contained additional argument (consistency by symmetry and a correct independence proof) repairs it, with no change of method or conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: is identical to the $n$-point Newton-Cotes rule with nodes $\xi_k$ (taking

issues.failure_explanation: Corollary cor:added-4 shows the construction yields exactly the n-point (closed) Newton-Cotes rule. For n=7 the weights are (41,216,27,272,27,216,41)h/140. Weddle's rule has weights 3h/10·(1,5,1,6,1,5,1) = (42,210,42,252,42,210,42)h/140. It is a different, integer-weight modification of that rule. It is exact only through degree 5, whereas the 7-point Newton-Cotes rule is exact through degree 7. So the construction does not recover Weddle's rule, contrary to the sentence.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'Weddle's' by 'the 7-point Newton-Cotes rule' and drop the identification with Weddle's rule.
issues.overall_effect: The sentence is a false verification claim. Only the identification with the 7-point Newton-Cotes rule is supported.
issues.title: Weddle's rule is not the 7-point Newton-Cotes rule, so it is not recovered
issues.why_classification: A one-phrase correction preserves all results and guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which, however, is no longer scalably exact or affinely exact on exponential

issues.failure_explanation: Write the logarithmic mean L=(f_0-f_1)/log(f_0/f_1) and note (f_0-f_1)log(f_0/f_1) = d^2/f + ... >= 0 with d=f_1-f_0. For the Gauss nodes, the expansion is q ≈ f(m) + (h^2/24) f'' − (h^2/18)(f'^2/f), while the exact value is f(m) + (h^2/24) f''. For f=e^x this gives q/h ≈ e^m(1 − h^2/72) versus the exact e^m(1 + h^2/24). The error is about h^3 f/18 times a nonzero factor, so the rule is O(h^3), not o(h^4). The correction needs the opposite sign, +(1/12)(f_0−f_1)log(f_0/f_1), to match through h^3. The stated claim of a Gauss-type o(h^4) two-point nonlinear formula is therefore false as written. The recomputation required is not a typo-level fix.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the sign of the correction term to +1/12 and verify the o(h^4) expansion for the Gauss nodes, restating the formula.
issues.overall_effect: The 'tantalizing glimpse' of nonlinear Gaussian quadrature rests on a formula that does not have the claimed order.
issues.title: Proposed 'o(h^4) two-point formula' has the wrong sign of the correction term and is only O(h^3)
issues.why_classification: A sign correction with a short expansion check restores the claim. It sits in the outlook and affects no theorem.
